idiom_name: per-concrete storage/DAO (sqlite_orm, SOCI) plus std::variant for mixed collections
implementation_notes: C++ ORMs map one struct to one table - sqlite_orm's make_storage/make_table and SOCI's rowset-into-struct - and no widely used library ships a concrete-table inheritance mapping: ODB's polymorphic support documents table-per-hierarchy, table-per-difference and table-per-class (joined on the key), not one table per concrete class. So the pattern is hand-written: one storage object, table definition and migration per concrete type with the base columns duplicated, and a std::variant (or a polymorphic handle) plus a UNION ALL query for mixed collections. The classic structure is still justified when leaf-scoped access dominates and you want to avoid the base-table join of class table inheritance; it is not worth it for small hierarchies that are usually read polymorphically.
pitfalls: The base columns are duplicated in every table, so a change to a shared field must be applied to each make_table/DAO and each migration by hand.
A std::variant of concrete types cannot express a reference to 'any subclass' row: an id alone is ambiguous across tables unless all keys come from one shared sequence.
sqlite_orm and SOCI do not join across the hierarchy, so a polymorphic read is a raw UNION ALL string you must keep in sync with the schema.
